name: agent-launch-with-run-in-background-should-deny
description: Live (agent-framework transcript line 210, toolu_016XTRyP2evsbryMPRU89k2M): main session called the Agent tool with `run_in_background: true` (subagent_type happened to be `implement-validator` here, but the bug is independent of subagent_type — ANY backgrounded Agent launch from the main session is the trigger). Hook decision: allow (gate: all-rules, 'All checks passed'). User reaction (line 225): 'how did you just run the implementer agent in the backround?? Dont we have a rule that is supposed to block you from this??? please kill that agent.' The user expects a rule that denies any backgrounded subagent spawn from the main session, regardless of subagent_type, because a backgrounded subagent keeps the active-subagents counter > 0 for the lifetime of its run, which makes `subagent-detector.checkCounterFallback` (src/utils/subagent-detector.ts:304) classify every subsequent main-session tool call as a subagent for the duration. Today no rule guards this; `subagent` rule (priority 20) only restricts what subagents may DO when they ARE running. The new `background-agent-block` rule (priority 25) deterministically fastDenies any Agent call with `run_in_background=true` from the main session, regardless of `subagent_type`.
